planner_plan.bridge_text: With Mosk’s name tucked safely in our hearts, the old fox shifted his weight. He looked at the narrow entrance, clearly expecting Lina to turn back toward the sunlight.

replacement_segments.text: Mosk pointed firmly at the door, his eyes dark and serious. Lina didn't budge. Instead, she reached into her pocket and pulled out the last apple of the season, a bright splash of red against the grey wood. She set it on the step between them and whispered that it was a gift for the trouble of walking her down. Mosk stared at the apple for a long time, his expression softening until he finally stood up, adjusted his green vest, and stepped onto the first stair.

At the bottom of the stairs, the humming grew into a quiet, pulsing song. There, nestled on a bed of moss, lay a firefly the size of a robin, her golden glow flickering like a dying candle. Mosk’s whiskers trembled as he looked at her. He whispered that she had been his friend once, but one winter long ago, he had failed to bring her the medicine she needed. Ever since that cold season, he had guarded the tree in silence, too ashamed to face her again.
